claim: Duvel Moortgat in Puurs-Sint-Amands (≈15 km from Duffel) runs a 2-hour guided brewery visit costing €18 including an introductory film, tour, pour initiation, two drinks and a gift; Saturday slots are at 11:00 and 14:00, but the bottling plant is not running on weekends.
quote: The visit lasts 2 hours and costs €18 per person. ... Tours run Monday-Friday at 1pm, 4pm, and 7pm (no 7pm Friday slots), plus Saturday at 11am and 2pm. ... The bottling plant is not operational on weekends or Friday nights.

claim: De Koninck's Antwerp City Brewery offers a self-paced, roughly 1-hour interactive tour at Mechelsesteenweg 291 with two tastings included, no guide required, wheelchair-accessible, and walkable from tram stops Harmonie/Merode.
quote: you visit at your own pace with a duration of about 1 hour, and 2 tasters are included, one before the tour and one during

claim: Het Anker in Mechelen runs guided 'Geniettour' visits through brewery, whisky aging warehouses and a rooftop with a Mechelen panorama, lasting about 1h45 with a tasting of 2 Gouden Carolus beers; the route has 100+ steps and no lift.
quote: a 'guided tour' through the brewery and whisky aging warehouses, plus 'a rooftop' visit overlooking Mechelen. You'll receive 'tasting of 2 Gouden Carolus beers' ... The experience includes 'more than 100 steps, no elevator is available'

claim: Public Het Anker tours run every Friday, Saturday and Sunday at 11:00; up to 4 people don't need to book in advance, and the price is €7.20 per person including two Gouden Carolus tastings.
quote: Guided tours are available every Friday, Saturday and Sunday at 11am; up to 4 persons do not need to book in advance. The price is €7.20 per person, which includes the guided tour and a tasting of 2 Gouden Carolus beers.

claim: Chocolatier Goossens in Antwerp (Isabellalei 6) was founded in 1955 by René Goossens and is run by two generations of maître chocolatiers who supply royal households and the American presidential gift list.
quote: Chocolaterie Goossens was founded in 1955 by Réne Goossens. 2 generations of real 'maître chocolatiers' with a passion for chocolate have managed to impress Royals, Presidents and Ambassadors around the globe.

claim: The Chocolate Line, Dominique Persoone's wildly experimental chocolatier (caipirinha, bacon, passion fruit bars), occupies the 1745 Palace of Meir on Antwerp's main shopping street and lets visitors watch chocolate being made in the back kitchen.
quote: The Antwerp location is located on the city's biggest shopping street 'the Meir' where they reside in 'The Palace Of the Meir,' a 1745 masterful building which Napoleon and King Willem I of the Netherlands had resided in.

claim: Chocolatier Burie on the Korte Gasthuisstraat is a family-run Antwerp institution since 1964, famous for monthly artistic window displays and for selling chocolate 'Antwerp Hands' alongside its pralines.
quote: In 1960, the shop moved to Antwerp, and in 1964 Hans Burie acquired and renamed a small shop, specializing in traditional chocolate making. ... The shop became legendary for its elaborate window displays, which change monthly.

claim: Kaasaffineurs Van Tricht's flagship 'Only Cheese' shop is at Boomgaardstraat 1-3 in Antwerp; the affineur has ripened cheeses since 2012 in the former bottling hall of De Koninck and has been called Europe's best cheese shop by the Wall Street Journal, even sending cheese to the ISS.
quote: The physical shop 'Only Cheese' is located at Boomgaardstraat 1-3 in Antwerp ... ripening cheeses since 2012 in the former bottling plant of city brewery De Koninck ... 'Best Cheese Shop in Europe' was voted by the Wall Street Journal, and astronauts of the International Space Station have taken cheeses aged by Van Tricht beyond Earth's atmosphere.

claim: Café Quinten Matsijs at Moriaanstraat 17 is documented as Antwerp's oldest tavern, occupying a building from 1565 with wood wainscoting, antique fireplace and stained glass, and counted Flemish writers Willem Elsschot and Paul van Ostaijen among its regulars.
quote: Café Quinten Matsijs is the oldest café in Antwerp, located at Moriaanstraat 17 in the historic city center. The building dates from 1565 ... Famous Flemish writers like Willem Elsschot and Paul van Ostaijen were regular guests.

claim: Café Den Engel on the Grote Markt is one of the most famous Antwerp brown cafés, open seven days a week from 09:00, renowned for pouring the city's best 'Bolleke' De Koninck at fair prices.
quote: Café Den Engel is one of the best brown cafés in Antwerp and perhaps the most famous one, open 7 days a week from 9 a.m. It's known for serving the best 'Bolleke' (a local beer style) in Antwerp

claim: Mechelen's Vismarkt, the historic 16th-century fish market beside the Dijle, is now the city's drinking and dining heart, lined with brown cafés, lounge bars and restaurants that stay busy late.
quote: This 16th century square is located next to the River Dijle and is well known and frequented by the locals. The Vismarkt (Fishmarket) has gone from a wholesaler and retailer of seafood to being the 'in central' of Mechelen

claim: 't Ankertje aan de Dijle at Vismarkt 20 is Het Anker brewery's city-centre tap and bottle shop in Mechelen, serving the full Gouden Carolus range in a convivial brown-café setting.
quote: This is the city centre outpost of the Het Anker Brewery and is a convivial, brown 'discussion café located on the Vismarkt, serving all of the brewery's beers, which it also sells in its bottle shop.

claim: The Saturday Exotische Markt fills Antwerp's Theaterplein from 08:00 to 16:00 with Mediterranean, North African and Turkish food stalls (msemen, shrimp/cheese kroketten, fresh feta pita, mint tea) — a daytime food crawl that pairs well with the rest of the city.
quote: Every Saturday morning, the Exotic Market takes place on Antwerp's Theaterplein. The market operates from 8am to 4pm on Saturdays.

claim: Mechelen's Saturday market runs every Saturday 08:00–13:00 across Grote Markt, Botermarkt, IJzerenleen and adjacent streets, with cheese, baked goods and Belgian waffles among the specialties (the Broodkraam stall is locally recommended).
quote: From 8 am to 1 pm, you can do your weekly shopping at the market, which spreads across Grote Markt, Botermarkt, IJzerenleen, and nearby streets.

claim: Caffènation, one of Antwerp's pioneer modern specialty coffee bars (20+ years old), runs its own roastery and four city venues (PAKT in Berchem, a 't Zuid clothing-store concept, two on Mechelsesteenweg), supplying bars and restaurants across Belgium.
quote: Twenty years ago, Caffènation was one of the first 'modern' coffee bars in Antwerp ... In Antwerp, they have four venues: one in PAKT in Berchem, one in a clothing store in 't Zuid, and two on Mechelsesteenweg.

claim: Normo is a micro-roastery and coffee bar in Antwerp's student quarter, roasting on a Loring Smartroaster under barista Jens Oris with a fair-trade, farmer-direct sourcing model.
quote: Normo approaches coffee from the viewpoint of sustainability and fairtrade coffee beans, building relationships with farmers across the globe ... Barista Jens Oris is at the helm, known for his meticulous roasting techniques using a state-of-the-art Loring Smartroaster

claim: Het Belofte Land on Begijnhofstraat in Lier (2 minutes from the UNESCO Begijnhof) is a small cosy café known for spaghetti and for serving coffee with the regional 'Lierse vlaai' and thick speculaas.
quote: Spaghetti is what the place is famous for ... After dinner they serve coffee with 'Lierse vlaai', a regional speciality
